title: The query log learns from kb/_self rule lookups: a miss becomes an anchored eval row or an alias
goal: A kb_ask row with root _self (a rag.py pack --root _self call or a kb_ask.py --root _self run) keeps root, verdict, tested, set, item, chars and answer_lines through querylog.py distill into the store's entries; learn turns a weak or none rules lookup into a finding of its own kind, with the answering line when the reader quoted one, and never a public gap or eval finding; apply turns an accepted rules finding into a kb/_self/_retrieval/lookup_eval.csv row anchored on a phrase of that line (or an aliases.csv row when the finding names a word pair), committed only when rag.py eval --root _self passes; the digest counts rules lookups, their verdicts and their printed chars apart from the public ones; a distill run on a copy of the spool shows the entries and findings
notes: Both checks pass before the work: querylog.py check pins the store's shape and rag.py eval --root _self pins that an apply-written row must resolve; the proof of the work is the distill run on a copy named in the goal, recorded in the report. Asked by the operator on 2026-10-06: the _self route must leave a log trace the self-improving pipeline can work on for accuracy and token efficiency; ST-dvf3xf52 writes the rows, this story makes distill, learn, apply and the digest read them.
